sections.h2: Where is the Pamlico County Tax Office and how do you reach it?
sections.html:
The Tax Office is in the Pamlico County Courthouse at 202 Main Street, Bayboro, NC 28515, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 538. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

Pamlico County combines the assessor and the tax collector into one office. It lists property, values it, tracks ownership changes and collects both current and delinquent tax. The Tax Administrator is appointed by the Board of Commissioners. Three direct lines split the work, and the office email is tax.office@pamlicocounty.org.

  • Listing (personal and business property): 252-745-3105
  • Collections and payment plans: 252-745-4125
  • Land Records: 252-745-3791
  • Fax: 252-745-4042

sections.h2: What is the Pamlico County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
The county posts a short list of fixed dates, and most of them repeat every year. January 1 fixes ownership, January 31 ends listing, and September 1 is the due date for annual bills.

  • January 1: the date property ownership is declared.
  • January 5: last day to pay the tax bill without interest.
  • January 31: last day of the listing period.
  • April: the Board of Equalization and Review opens for appeals.
  • May 31: last day to pay delinquent taxes before they are advertised in the newspaper.
  • June 1: last day to submit exemption and exclusion applications.
  • July: annual tax bills are mailed.
  • September 1: annual bills are due.

The state fixes the interest rules that follow a missed date: 2% from January 6 until February 1, then three-fourths of one percent for each month or part of a month after that.

sections.h2: When is the next Pamlico County reappraisal?
sections.html:
The last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2020. The county's pages give two different dates for the next one, January 1, 2026 on its About the Tax Office page and January 1, 2027 in the key dates list, so confirm the date that applies with the Tax Office at 252-745-3105.

North Carolina requires every county to reappraise real property at least once every eight years, and the county calls its schedule the Octennial Plan. The Assessor works from market value as of the effective date, and in between reappraisals values do not follow the market year to year. The county holds more than 17,000 parcels of real property, along with business personal property, mobile homes and aircraft that must be valued as well.

sections.h2: What are the Pamlico County property tax rates?
sections.html:
The county rate page lists 0.7000 for the county in 2026, against 0.645 in 2025. Towns and fire districts add their own rates on top, so the bill depends on where the parcel sits.

Pamlico County has 12 tax districts, and the money pays for schools, roads, police and fire protection. The county's worked example multiplies a $100,000 value by the town and fire rate per hundred dollars for a house in Bayboro in the Triangle Fire District. Call the Tax Office to confirm which rates apply to your parcel and whether the figures below are final for the year.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Pamlico County value?
sections.html:
Ask for a hearing from the Board of Equalization and Review in writing before it adjourns. The Tax Administrator serves as clerk to the board, and requests go to P.O. Box 538, Bayboro, NC 28515.

For 2026 the board convened April 8, adjourned May 12 and set 5:00 p.m. on May 11 as the last time to file, so that window has closed. The county's real estate appeal form is labeled for a January through May timeframe. At the board, the taxpayer carries the burden of showing the value or location was wrong or that the property was taxed in error. A decision can then go to the state Property Tax Commission by written notice within 30 days of the date the board mailed its decision.

sections.h2: What property tax relief programs does Pamlico County offer?
sections.html:
The county posts applications for the three state programs, with instructions: the elderly or disabled exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment and the disabled veteran exemption. It also offers forms for present use value, a general exemption and a business property exemption.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or half of appraised value, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled, within the state income limit of $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4.0% of income at or below the limit and 5.0% up to 150% of it, with the extra deferred as a lien.

Applications are due by June 1 on the county calendar. With 34.9% of residents 65 or older, these programs reach a large share of owners, so anyone who may qualify should call the Listing line before the deadline.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when a Pamlico County house is sold?
sections.html:
Any unpaid tax stays with the property, so it is settled at or before closing. State law makes the yearly tax a lien from the listing date, and interest, penalties and costs attach at the same time.

Before choosing a closing date, call Collections at 252-745-4125 for the current balance. The county lists May 31 as the last day to pay delinquent taxes before they are advertised in the newspaper. Tax foreclosure under state procedure ends in a sale at the courthouse door. A seller pays the deed excise tax to the register of deeds at $1 for each $500 of value, and a closing attorney normally collects both amounts from proceeds. If the sale needs to happen quickly, give your attorney the tax bill early.

sections.h2: What does Pamlico County look like in the census numbers?
sections.html:
Pamlico County is small and rural. The Census Bureau estimates 12,758 residents for July 1, 2025, up 4.0% since the April 2020 base, on 336.52 square miles of land.

The owner-occupied rate is 82.9%, the median owner-occupied value is $216,800 and median gross rent is $752. The county has 5,456 households and 7,610 housing units, and 34.9% of residents are 65 or older. Median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $59,717 and 17.6% of people live in poverty.

faqs.q: When are Pamlico County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Annual bills are due September 1 and are mailed in July. The county lists January 5 as the last day to pay without interest.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Pamlico County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call Collections at 252-745-4125 for payments and payment plans, or Listing at 252-745-3105 for personal and business property. The office is at 202 Main Street, Bayboro.

faqs.q: What is the Pamlico County tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate page lists 0.7000 for the county in 2026, plus separate town and fire district rates. Ask the Tax Office to confirm the rates that apply to your parcel.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Pamlico County assessment?
faqs.a: The 2026 filing deadline was 5:00 p.m. on May 11, 2026, and the board adjourned May 12. Ask the Tax Office when the next board opens, which the county lists as April.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for tax relief applications in Pamlico County?
faqs.a: The county lists June 1 as the last day to submit exemption and exclusion applications. Use the Listing line at 252-745-3105 for forms and help.
